03Mathematical logic and foundations

Logic and set algebra

logic-and-sets

Prove set identities and image statements, Finset cardinality facts and equivalence relations.

How to run itHow checking works

What the agent does

The agent gets a working directory with a Lean file, Solution.lean, and a problem in words. It edits the file until it compiles and is correct. Tasks are generated from a seed and a difficulty from 1 to 3, so the supply is unlimited and every task is new.

An example task

Instruction, as the agent sees it

Prove properties of a relation

Prove the following.

On the integers define x∼y  ⟺  7∣x−yx \sim y \iff 7 \mid x - yx∼y⟺7∣x−y. Prove that ∼\sim∼ is an equivalence relation.

What to do

Solution.lean in the working directory states the theorem in Lean 4 with Mathlib, with sorry in place of the proof. Replace every sorry with a proof.

  • Do not change the statement of any theorem or any definition the file gives you. You may add your own lemmas and definitions.
  • Check your work with lake env lean Solution.lean (run it inside /opt/arena/lean, giving the full path to the file). It must compile without errors.
  • A theorem counts only if its proof is complete: no sorry, no new axioms, no native_decide.
  • The reward is 1 if the theorem is proved and 0 otherwise.
Solution.leanthe file the agent starts from
import Mathlib

/-- The relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. -/
theorem rel_equiv :
    Equivalence (fun x y : ℤ => 7 ∣ x - y) := by
  sorry
Show a reference solution
import Mathlib

/-- The relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. -/
theorem rel_equiv :
    Equivalence (fun x y : ℤ => 7 ∣ x - y) := ⟨fun x => by omega, fun {x y} h => by omega, fun {x y z} h1 h2 => by omega⟩

Reference solutions are never shown to the agent. They are compiled in the environment's self-test, so every task has at least one proof that passes.

The families

Each task belongs to one family: a different piece of the area's work.

finset card
theorem card_fact (s t : Finset ℕ) :
    ((s ∪ t).image (fun x : ℕ => 9 * x + 4)).card + ((s ∩ t).image (fun x : ℕ => 9 * x + 4)).card = s.card + t.card
relations
theorem rel_equiv :
    Equivalence (fun x y : ℤ => 9 ∣ x ^ 2 - y ^ 2)
set identities
theorem image_identity {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (A : Set β) :
    f '' (f ⁻¹' A) = A ∩ Set.range f

Reward

Range
0 to 1
Checked by
Lean kernel
Deterministic
yes

Every theorem must be stated exactly as given and proved: no sorry, no new axioms, no native_decide. The reward is the share of theorems that pass. A file that does not compile scores 0. The submission is also re-checked by a second kernel run. Read how checking works.

How to run it

1. Set up the Lean projectLean 4.29.1 with Mathlib 5e932f97dd
git clone https://github.com/RenaissanceLabs-EU/lean-arena && cd lean-arena
cd lean && lake exe cache get
2. Generate a taskseed and difficulty pick the task
python3 tools/make_task.py logic_and_sets --seed 7 --difficulty 2 --out /tmp/task
3. Grade a solutionprints the reward
python3 arena/grade.py --spec /tmp/task/spec.json --solution /tmp/task/Solution.lean

Tasks are also exported as Harbor task folders (instruction.md, task.toml, tests/), the format used by several RL frameworks, with the image built from the Lean project.

How hard is it?

A floor, not a ceiling: how many sampled tasks a single automation call can close with no thought at all. Each theorem was given the tactic first | grind | aesop | simp | omega | norm_num | nlinarith | decide. A task counts as closed only if every theorem in it is. Overall 5 of 24. The rest need a real proof.
